message.content:
READ-ONLY diagnosis of the Nxeon migration engine at /opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-real.ts (~6600 lines). Do NOT modify files. Return root cause with file:line + concrete minimal fix.

## Problem
Compose project `/opt/soulpilates-staging` fails to come up with:
`Conflict. The container name "/soulpilates-mongo" is already in use by container "<id>". You have to remove (or rename) that container to be able to reuse that name.`

Two migrated compose projects — `/opt/soulpilates` (prod) and `/opt/soulpilates-staging` — both hardcode `container_name: soulpilates-mongo` (and likely other shared names). Compose's `container_name:` is an ABSOLUTE name that overrides the normal `<project>_<service>` prefixing, so when the second project's `docker compose up` runs, the name already exists from the first project → hard conflict → the whole staging stack fails.

Note: these two are near-clones (prod + staging of the same app). On the SOURCE they presumably ran without conflict because staging used different container_names OR was not running. Determine which.

## Investigate (cite file:line)
1. The compose bring-up loop (~5354-5410) — how it iterates composeDirs and runs `compose up`. Does it detect name conflicts before/after? What does it do on failure (the settle + running-count check added recently)?
2. Whether the engine could detect duplicate `container_name:` values ACROSS the migrated compose projects and handle it: options — (a) bring up only one of the conflicting clones and clearly report the other as "duplicate of <dir>, not started — it reuses the same container names as <dir>"; (b) for the second project, run compose with an override that drops/uniquifies container_name (risky — changes app expectations); (c) detect and skip with an honest, specific message rather than a raw docker error.
3. Read the run: from /opt/nxeon: `node -e 'const {PrismaClient}=require("@prisma/client");const p=new PrismaClient();p.migration.findUnique({where:{id:"cmsciv67q0005hlhwo5vzzu7h"},select:{items:true,log:true}}).then(r=>{console.log((r.log||"").split("\n").filter(l=>/compose|Compose|container name|Conflict|soulpilates/i.test(l)).join("\n"))})'`

## Deliverable
Recommend the SAFEST correct behavior and give a concrete minimal fix with file:line. My lean: detect duplicate container_name across composeDirs BEFORE bring-up; bring up the first project that owns a name, and for any later project sharing ≥1 container_name, do NOT attempt it — report a precise, honest step ("/opt/soulpilates-staging reuses container names already taken by /opt/soulpilates — these are the same app's prod+staging; migrate/run them on separate hosts, or rename container_name in its compose file"). Explain how to read container_name values on the target (e.g. `docker compose -f <files> config` or YAML grep) and where to insert the check. Be concrete; do not propose auto-rewriting the customer's compose file.
